{"records":[{"id":"S01","section":"SUMMARY","text":"In B. N. Muttoo and another v. T. K. Nandi, Civil Appeal No. 2302 of 1977, the Supreme Court of India considered the landlord's appeal by special leave against the Delhi High Court's order allowing the respondent-tenant's revision, setting aside the Rent Controller's eviction order, and remanding the proceedings. The principal dispute concerned whether Muttoo could invoke the special possession entitlement under section 14A(1) of the Delhi Rent Control Act, 1958, despite having retired from Government service before receiving the Government's notice to vacate his allotted accommodation and before filing his eviction petition. The Supreme Court allowed the landlord's appeal and held that retirement before service of the Government notice did not, by itself, exclude the landlord from section 14A benefits.","status":"SUPREME_COURT_ADOPTED_DISPOSITION_AND_COURT_RECORDED_PROCEDURAL_HISTORY","stage":"Supreme Court appeal and final disposition","actor_ids":["1187427/478b87d079850360/A01","1187427/478b87d079850360/A02","1187427/478b87d079850360/A04","1187427/478b87d079850360/A05","1187427/478b87d079850360/A06"],"property_ids":["1187427/478b87d079850360/P01","1187427/478b87d079850360/P02"],"event_ids":["1187427/478b87d079850360/E01","1187427/478b87d079850360/E02","1187427/478b87d079850360/E03","1187427/478b87d079850360/E05","1187427/478b87d079850360/E06","1187427/478b87d079850360/E07"],"refs":["IK-1187427:L234","IK-1187427:L236","IK-1187427:L241","IK-1187427:L249","IK-1187427:L286","IK-1187427:L343"],"role_bindings":[{"role":"LANDLORD","actor_id":"1187427/478b87d079850360/A01"},{"role":"TENANT","actor_id":"1187427/478b87d079850360/A02"},{"role":"ISSUING_COURT","actor_id":"1187427/478b87d079850360/A06"},{"role":"REPORTING_COURT","actor_id":"1187427/478b87d079850360/A06"}]},{"id":"S02","section":"GROUND","text":"B. N. Muttoo, the appellant-landlord and former Inspector General of Police, leased property No. F-9, East of Kailash, New Delhi, to T. K. Nandi from 15 September 1972 at a monthly rent of Rs. 2,200, excluding electricity and water charges. The lease permitted residential and/or professional purposes but excluded commercial purposes. Following renewals, Nandi became a monthly tenant under the Delhi Rent Control Act. This F-9 property was the tenanted property from which Muttoo sought recovery of possession. It was distinct from the Government-allotted accommodation at C-II/77, Moti Bagh I, New Delhi, which Muttoo occupied while in Government service.","status":"COURT_RECORDED_FACT","stage":"Underlying tenancy and property identification","actor_ids":["1187427/478b87d079850360/A01","1187427/478b87d079850360/A02","1187427/478b87d079850360/A03"],"property_ids":["1187427/478b87d079850360/P01","1187427/478b87d079850360/P02"],"event_ids":[],"refs":["IK-1187427:L244","IK-1187427:L246"],"role_bindings":[{"role":"LANDLORD","actor_id":"1187427/478b87d079850360/A01"},{"role":"TENANT","actor_id":"1187427/478b87d079850360/A02"},{"role":"REPORTING_COURT","actor_id":"1187427/478b87d079850360/A06"}]},{"id":"S03","section":"GROUND","text":"On 18 July 1974, Muttoo filed an earlier eviction petition against Nandi alleging misuse, subletting, and bona fide requirement. That petition was registered as Suit No. 182 of 1974 and remained pending when the Supreme Court judgment recorded its procedural history. The filing and pendency were recorded facts; the allegations underlying that earlier petition were not independently established or finally adjudicated by the Supreme Court in this appeal.","status":"COURT_RECORDED_PROCEDURAL_HISTORY_WITH_UNADJUDICATED_PARTY_ALLEGATIONS","stage":"Earlier eviction proceeding","actor_ids":["1187427/478b87d079850360/A01","1187427/478b87d079850360/A02"],"property_ids":["1187427/478b87d079850360/P01"],"event_ids":["1187427/478b87d079850360/E04"],"refs":["IK-1187427:L245","IK-1187427:L280","IK-1187427:L324"],"role_bindings":[{"role":"LANDLORD","actor_id":"1187427/478b87d079850360/A01"},{"role":"TENANT","actor_id":"1187427/478b87d079850360/A02"},{"role":"REPORTING_COURT","actor_id":"1187427/478b87d079850360/A06"}]},{"id":"S04","section":"GROUND","text":"The Central Government adopted a policy decision on 9 September 1975 requiring Government servants who owned houses in the relevant Delhi area to vacate Government accommodation allotted to them within three months beginning 1 October 1975. The judgment describes this decision as the policy background for the subsequent statutory amendment. The policy concerned Government servants, whereas the enacted section 14A used the broader expression 'person'.","status":"COURT_RECORDED_GOVERNMENT_DECISION_AND_SUPREME_COURT_ADOPTED_STATUTORY_DISTINCTION","stage":"Government policy and legislative background","actor_ids":["1187427/478b87d079850360/A03","1187427/478b87d079850360/A06"],"property_ids":["1187427/478b87d079850360/P02"],"event_ids":[],"refs":["IK-1187427:L246","IK-1187427:L276","IK-1187427:L278","IK-1187427:L288","IK-1187427:L291","IK-1187427:L305"],"role_bindings":[{"role":"NOTICE_AUTHORITY","actor_id":"1187427/478b87d079850360/A03"},{"role":"REPORTING_COURT","actor_id":"1187427/478b87d079850360/A06"}]},{"id":"S05","section":"GROUND","text":"Muttoo retired as Inspector General of Police on 30 November 1975. While in office, he had occupied Government-allotted premises at C-II/77, Moti Bagh I, New Delhi. On 9 December 1975, a notice was served on him by the Deputy Director (Administration), referring to the Government's Office Memorandum dated 9 September 1975 and requiring qualifying Government officials who owned houses in Delhi or New Delhi to vacate their allotted Government residences before the stipulated deadline. The notice warned that noncompliance would attract a penal or market-rate licence charge and necessary eviction action. The judgment establishes the notice and its stated consequences, not that Muttoo actually paid such charges or that the Government completed eviction from its accommodation.","status":"COURT_RECORDED_RETIREMENT_AND_GOVERNMENT_NOTICE_WITH_CONDITIONAL_CONSEQUENCES","stage":"Retirement and Government accommodation notice","actor_ids":["1187427/478b87d079850360/A01","1187427/478b87d079850360/A03"],"property_ids":["1187427/478b87d079850360/P02"],"event_ids":["1187427/478b87d079850360/E01","1187427/478b87d079850360/E02"],"refs":["IK-1187427:L246","IK-1187427:L247","IK-1187427:L248","IK-1187427:L279"],"role_bindings":[{"role":"LANDLORD","actor_id":"1187427/478b87d079850360/A01"},{"role":"NOTICE_AUTHORITY","actor_id":"1187427/478b87d079850360/A03"},{"role":"REPORTING_COURT","actor_id":"1187427/478b87d079850360/A06"}]},{"id":"S06","section":"GROUND","text":"On 9 December 1975, the same day that the Government notice was served, Muttoo instituted the present eviction proceeding against Nandi under section 14A(1). Nandi applied for leave to defend on 16 January 1976. On 10 March 1976, the Rent Controller refused leave to defend and decreed eviction in favour of the landlord. The Rent Controller treated the landlord's retirement status at the dates of notice and application as irrelevant to eligibility under the statutory requirements, viewed section 14A as a distinct cause of action from the earlier petition, and rejected the argument that mixed residential and professional letting prevented relief under the special provision. These were the Rent Controller's determinations, not independent Supreme Court findings on every aspect of the underlying facts.","status":"PROCEDURAL_HISTORY_AND_REPORTED_RENT_CONTROLLER_REASONING","stage":"Section 14A petition and Rent Controller decision","actor_ids":["1187427/478b87d079850360/A01","1187427/478b87d079850360/A02","1187427/478b87d079850360/A04"],"property_ids":["1187427/478b87d079850360/P01"],"event_ids":["1187427/478b87d079850360/E03","1187427/478b87d079850360/E05"],"refs":["IK-1187427:L241","IK-1187427:L248","IK-1187427:L280","IK-1187427:L282","IK-1187427:L283","IK-1187427:L284"],"role_bindings":[{"role":"LANDLORD","actor_id":"1187427/478b87d079850360/A01"},{"role":"TENANT","actor_id":"1187427/478b87d079850360/A02"},{"role":"ISSUING_COURT","actor_id":"1187427/478b87d079850360/A04"},{"role":"REPORTING_COURT","actor_id":"1187427/478b87d079850360/A06"}]},{"id":"S07","section":"COUNTERARGUMENT","text":"In seeking leave to contest Muttoo's section 14A eviction petition, Nandi raised three principal objections. First, he argued that Muttoo could not use the special procedure under section 25B because Muttoo was no longer a Government servant when the petition was filed. Second, he asserted that the pending 1974 eviction proceeding prevented the later proceeding because the same ground was already before the Rent Controller. Third, he contended that the F-9 premises had been let for residential and professional purposes rather than exclusively residential use, and therefore the landlord could not obtain eviction on the asserted ground. These propositions were the tenant's objections; the Court did not adopt their claimed legal consequences.","status":"TENANT_SUBMISSION_REPORTED_BY_SUPREME_COURT","stage":"Tenant's application for leave to contest","actor_ids":["1187427/478b87d079850360/A01","1187427/478b87d079850360/A02","1187427/478b87d079850360/A04"],"property_ids":["1187427/478b87d079850360/P01"],"event_ids":["1187427/478b87d079850360/E03","1187427/478b87d079850360/E04","1187427/478b87d079850360/E05"],"refs":["IK-1187427:L122","IK-1187427:L123","IK-1187427:L124","IK-1187427:L125","IK-1187427:L129","IK-1187427:L130","IK-1187427:L131","IK-1187427:L132","IK-1187427:L133","IK-1187427:L134","IK-1187427:L135","IK-1187427:L280","IK-1187427:L281"],"role_bindings":[{"role":"LANDLORD","actor_id":"1187427/478b87d079850360/A01"},{"role":"TENANT","actor_id":"1187427/478b87d079850360/A02"},{"role":"REPORTING_COURT","actor_id":"1187427/478b87d079850360/A06"}]},{"id":"S08","section":"COUNTERARGUMENT","text":"The Delhi High Court accepted Nandi's revision and set aside the Rent Controller's eviction order, remanding the proceedings to the Rent Controller for disposal according to law. Its principal contrary conclusion was that Muttoo had retired on 30 November 1975, before the amending Ordinance became operative on 1 December 1975, and was consequently liable to vacate Government accommodation independently of his ownership of the disputed tenanted property. On that reasoning, the High Court considered the section 14A eviction application unavailable to him. The remand was ordered by the High Court, not by the Supreme Court. The Supreme Court subsequently rejected the High Court's restrictive statutory interpretation.","status":"REPORTED_HIGH_COURT_ORDER_AND_REJECTED_HIGH_COURT_LEGAL_REASONING","stage":"Delhi High Court revision and remand","actor_ids":["1187427/478b87d079850360/A01","1187427/478b87d079850360/A02","1187427/478b87d079850360/A04","1187427/478b87d079850360/A05","1187427/478b87d079850360/A06"],"property_ids":["1187427/478b87d079850360/P01","1187427/478b87d079850360/P02"],"event_ids":["1187427/478b87d079850360/E01","1187427/478b87d079850360/E05","1187427/478b87d079850360/E06"],"refs":["IK-1187427:L236","IK-1187427:L241","IK-1187427:L249","IK-1187427:L267","IK-1187427:L285","IK-1187427:L286","IK-1187427:L307"],"role_bindings":[{"role":"LANDLORD","actor_id":"1187427/478b87d079850360/A01"},{"role":"TENANT","actor_id":"1187427/478b87d079850360/A02"},{"role":"ISSUING_COURT","actor_id":"1187427/478b87d079850360/A05"},{"role":"REPORTING_COURT","actor_id":"1187427/478b87d079850360/A06"}]},{"id":"S09","section":"GROUND","text":"Section 14A(1), as reproduced and interpreted by the Supreme Court, confers a special right on a landlord who is a person occupying residential premises allotted by the Central Government or a local authority and who is required, by or pursuant to a general or special order of that authority, to vacate the allotted accommodation or incur specified obligations in default because the landlord owns residential accommodation in Delhi in the landlord's own name or in the name of a wife or dependent child. When the statutory requirements are satisfied, the right to recover possession of premises let out by that landlord accrues from the qualifying order. The Court identified these requirements as the operative statutory test. This statement describes the adopted test and its conditional legal effect; it does not constitute a separate independent finding that every input to a formal rule calculation has been verified.","status":"SUPREME_COURT_ADOPTED_STATUTORY_INTERPRETATION_WITH_CONDITIONAL_ENTITLEMENT","stage":"Supreme Court analysis of section 14A eligibility","actor_ids":["1187427/478b87d079850360/A01","1187427/478b87d079850360/A03","1187427/478b87d079850360/A06"],"property_ids":["1187427/478b87d079850360/P01","1187427/478b87d079850360/P02"],"event_ids":["1187427/478b87d079850360/E02","1187427/478b87d079850360/E03"],"refs":["IK-1187427:L268","IK-1187427:L270","IK-1187427:L286","IK-1187427:L287","IK-1187427:L288"],"role_bindings":[{"role":"LANDLORD","actor_id":"1187427/478b87d079850360/A01"},{"role":"NOTICE_AUTHORITY","actor_id":"1187427/478b87d079850360/A03"},{"role":"REPORTING_COURT","actor_id":"1187427/478b87d079850360/A06"}]},{"id":"S10","section":"GROUND","text":"The Supreme Court rejected the proposition that section 14A benefits were confined to persons still serving as Government employees. The enacted provision used the word 'person' rather than 'Government servant', and the Court held that this choice could not be treated as inadvertent or read down to the narrower class covered by the Government's policy. Government-allotted accommodation was not restricted to serving officials, and the legislative purpose was to facilitate recovery of Government accommodation by enabling qualifying allottees to recover premises they had let to tenants. Consequently, Muttoo's retirement before receiving the Government notice did not by itself bar the statutory benefit. The Court expressly declined to agree with the High Court on this issue.","status":"SUPREME_COURT_ADOPTED_LEGAL_REASONING_REJECTING_HIGH_COURT_RESTRICTION","stage":"Supreme Court statutory interpretation of retirement objection","actor_ids":["1187427/478b87d079850360/A01","1187427/478b87d079850360/A03","1187427/478b87d079850360/A05","1187427/478b87d079850360/A06"],"property_ids":["1187427/478b87d079850360/P01","1187427/478b87d079850360/P02"],"event_ids":["1187427/478b87d079850360/E01","1187427/478b87d079850360/E02","1187427/478b87d079850360/E06","1187427/478b87d079850360/E07"],"refs":["IK-1187427:L288","IK-1187427:L299","IK-1187427:L300","IK-1187427:L301","IK-1187427:L305","IK-1187427:L306","IK-1187427:L307","IK-1187427:L343"],"role_bindings":[{"role":"LANDLORD","actor_id":"1187427/478b87d079850360/A01"},{"role":"NOTICE_AUTHORITY","actor_id":"1187427/478b87d079850360/A03"},{"role":"ISSUING_COURT","actor_id":"1187427/478b87d079850360/A06"},{"role":"REPORTING_COURT","actor_id":"1187427/478b87d079850360/A06"}]},{"id":"S11","section":"COUNTERARGUMENT","text":"The Supreme Court acknowledged that the Government circular of 9 September 1975 and the individual notice served on Muttoo supported a narrower Government-servant-focused policy account. It also recognized why the High Court's interpretation could appear understandable in light of that policy. Nevertheless, the Court treated the enacted language of section 14A as controlling and refused to restrict 'person' to serving Government servants. The Government policy was therefore relevant contrary interpretive material, not a statutory condition independently excluding retired allottees.","status":"SUPREME_COURT_ANALYSIS_OF_CONTRARY_MATERIAL_NOT_ADOPTED_AS_STATUTORY_RESTRICTION","stage":"Supreme Court consideration of Government policy and contrary interpretation","actor_ids":["1187427/478b87d079850360/A01","1187427/478b87d079850360/A03","1187427/478b87d079850360/A05","1187427/478b87d079850360/A06"],"property_ids":["1187427/478b87d079850360/P02"],"event_ids":["1187427/478b87d079850360/E02","1187427/478b87d079850360/E06"],"refs":["IK-1187427:L168","IK-1187427:L169","IK-1187427:L170","IK-1187427:L174","IK-1187427:L175","IK-1187427:L288","IK-1187427:L290","IK-1187427:L291","IK-1187427:L292","IK-1187427:L299","IK-1187427:L305"],"role_bindings":[{"role":"LANDLORD","actor_id":"1187427/478b87d079850360/A01"},{"role":"NOTICE_AUTHORITY","actor_id":"1187427/478b87d079850360/A03"},{"role":"REPORTING_COURT","actor_id":"1187427/478b87d079850360/A06"}]},{"id":"S12","section":"COUNTERARGUMENT","text":"The Supreme Court addressed Nihal Chand v. Kalyan Chand Jain as a reported precedent that had expressed some sympathy for restricting section 14A benefits in cases involving retired or transferred Government servants. The earlier case did not finally decide the question presented here. As described in the present judgment, its relevant notice had been served before retirement, so entitlement could be explained by the right arising while the landlord was still in service. In Muttoo's case the notice was served after retirement. The Supreme Court accordingly confronted a materially different timing question and resolved it through the enacted meaning of 'person'.","status":"SUPREME_COURT_TREATMENT_AND_DISTINCTION_OF_REPORTED_PRECEDENT","stage":"Supreme Court treatment of Nihal Chand precedent","actor_ids":["1187427/478b87d079850360/A01","1187427/478b87d079850360/A06"],"property_ids":["1187427/478b87d079850360/P02"],"event_ids":["1187427/478b87d079850360/E01","1187427/478b87d079850360/E02"],"refs":["IK-1187427:L292","IK-1187427:L296","IK-1187427:L297","IK-1187427:L298","IK-1187427:L301","IK-1187427:L305"],"role_bindings":[{"role":"LANDLORD","actor_id":"1187427/478b87d079850360/A01"},{"role":"REPORTING_COURT","actor_id":"1187427/478b87d079850360/A06"}]},{"id":"S13","section":"COUNTERARGUMENT","text":"Nandi's mixed-use objection depended on the distinction between premises let for residential purposes alone and premises let for residential as well as professional purposes. The Supreme Court accepted that the F-9 lease included both residential and professional purposes, but distinguished section 14A from section 14(1)(e). The Court explained that section 14A focuses on residential accommodation owned by the landlord and does not repeat section 14(1)(e)'s residential-letting requirement. The F-9 premises had been constructed under the Delhi Development Authority's residential scheme, and their residential character was not lost merely because the lease permitted professional use.
